The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It uses only es-toolkit (from its `compat` entry), with no hand-written replacements and no lodash import.

- **Functions:** `applyPatch` uses `merge`, `toTitle` uses `startCase`, and `preview` uses `truncate` with `{ length: 24 }`. The exported names, signatures and `Row`/`Config` types are unchanged.
- **Why `compat`:** The root es-toolkit `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word (`HELLO WORLD` → `Hello World`), while lodash keeps it (`HELLO WORLD`). The `compat` version matches lodash. The root `merge` also differed from lodash in 176 of 60,006 test cases, so I used the `compat` `merge` as well.

- **Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 4044 bytes (min+gzip) and 97 bytes of own code. I did not measure the original bundle, because `lodash` isn't in `node_modules`, so the original cannot be bundled here. Importing from the `compat` barrel works; the individual subpaths I tried don't resolve.

`src/module.ts` is unchanged and still imports lodash. Because lodash isn't installed, `tsc -p` over the whole project fails on that file (TS2307), which was already the case before this change. I didn't touch `package.json`, since the task said not to install anything.
